sources.note: Nothing. Section 'Phonology' infers 8 consonants (m n p t k ʔ β ɾ) and 5-6 vowels plus two diphthongs from 'Vincent (n.d.) 97 terms for Kambaira'; discusses sound changes shared with North Tairora and Binumarien loans; no word for stress, accent, tone or pitch anywhere on the page. sources.note: No prose at all. IPA transcriptions of eight body-part nouns (eye, ear, nose, tongue, teeth, knee, blood; 'hand' left blank) in six possessor frames (mi/yumi/yu/yupela/em/ol) carry primary (ˈ) and secondary (ˌ) stress marks, e.g. ˈɛniˌbumi 'my eye', ˈeja ˈami 'my ear', ˈena ʔiˈʔonde 'my knee', ˈena ˈbitiˌʔɛh 'my blood', ˈʔaʔa kiˈbumi 'their eye', ˈʔaʔa qaˈʔami 'their ear', ˈmenə ʔaˈʔami 'his ear'.
